title: Sunday Ticket
summary: Work out which four NFL games to put on the multiview, then watch every one of your players score on the same board.
body: Sunday Ticket answers one question: given every league you play in, which NFL games have the most of your players in them? It reads your rosters, works out where your starters actually are on a Sunday, and ranks the games so the four boxes on your multiview are the four worth having.

body.heading: Reading the board
items: Your matchup, up top. One card per league — your crest against your opponent's, both live scores, and how many starters each of you still has left to play. In both leagues, you get both cards.

Game boxes, below. One per NFL game in the window, ordered by how much of your roster is in it. Each player row shows his live fantasy points in that league's scoring, so the same player can carry two different numbers.
The Updated pill. When the board last actually heard from MFL. A board that says "live" and has not been confirmed since noon is not live, and the pill is how you tell.

body: The numbers refresh about once a minute while games are being played, then back off once everything is final. Lose your connection mid-afternoon and the scores you already have stay put rather than blanking out — a stale number with a timestamp on it beats a blank one.

body.heading: Two things it deliberately will not do
items: Leagues from outside this site show projections only. We can read your rosters there, but not their live scoring — those cards say Projections only rather than quietly showing you zeroes.
It is the wide shot, not the box score. For scoring plays, the ticker and the full breakdown, Live Scoring is still the deep cut.

body: Your country and clock preferences change what Sunday Ticket prints beside each game — kickoff times in your own clock, and the TV channel for where you actually live. Both are set on Preferences.

title: MFL Football
summary: Every team you own, in every MyFantasyLeague league, scoring on one page — then tap a league to see the whole thing: all its matchups, its standings, and the week's top scorers.
body: Every other scoreboard on this site shows you one league. MFL Football shows you all of them: sign in once with your MyFantasyLeague account and it reads every league that account plays in — this league, the other one, and the ones nobody here has ever heard of — then puts every matchup on a single page. It lives at its own address rather than under a league, because it does not belong to one.

body.heading: What's on the board
items: The NFL games strip, up top. The whole week's real games with live scores and clocks, so you can see what is still to come before you look at what it did to you.
One panel per league. Your matchup, both live totals, projected finals, how many starters each side has left, and a bar showing your share of the win. Doubleheader weeks show both games.

Tap a matchup for the lineups. Both teams, starters first in QB, RB, WR, TE, K, DEF order with several of a position grouped together, then the bench underneath with its own total — what you left on it, which is a different question from what you scored.

Scoring, across everything. A running list of every play that scored you points in any league. The same touchdown can appear more than once, and that is the point: one player started in three leagues really is three pieces of news.
Red zone. When one of your players' teams has the ball inside the twenty, it says so, and names who you have in the drive.

body.heading: Open the whole league
items: Tap a league's name at the top of its panel. The board you have been reading shows your own matchup; this opens that league's full board — every matchup in it, not just yours.
Your game still leads. The rest follow closest-first, so the game worth watching is the one at the top. Your own matchup is the only one badged, because most of the cards are nobody's.

Scores or Standings. Two buttons under the week. Standings are MyFantasyLeague's own table, in MyFantasyLeague's own order — records there update when games go final, not with the live scores beside them, and the table says so.

Top teams and top performances. Under the scores: who is putting up the week's numbers across the whole league, and the individual games behind it. Bench players never appear — those are points nobody can score.

body: This works for the outside leagues too — the ones this site does not run. Their standings and scores come straight from MyFantasyLeague with your own sign-in, so a league nobody here has heard of gets the same full board as this one.

body.heading: Crests and names
items: Teams in this league and the other one wear the crests you already know.

A team in an outside league whose name is a real NFL club — Cowboys, Chiefs, New Orleans Saints — gets that club's mark automatically. The match has to be exact, because a wrong crest is worse than none: The Boondock Saints is not the Saints.
Everyone else gets their initials. Nothing is guessed.

body: Switch leagues off in the board's own settings and it stops reading them altogether, which is what keeps a Sunday quick when you are in six of them. The choice is remembered on that device, so your phone and your laptop can watch different sets.

Scores refresh on their own while games are being played and ease off once everything is final. The pill beside the week number says when the board last actually heard from MyFantasyLeague — a page that says "live" but has not been confirmed in an hour is not live, and that is how you tell.

title: MFL Football on Google TV
summary: Put your fantasy score, win chance and lineups on top of the game you're watching, and jump to the games your players are in.
body: The MFL Football TV app does two things. Opened on its own, it shows the full broadcast board. Its Score overlay tile draws a see-through panel over whatever you're watching, such as YouTube TV, so you can follow your matchups without leaving the game. The app is in testing right now, so getting it takes one extra step.

body.heading: Get the app
items: Send Brandon your TV's Google account. That's the Gmail address signed in on your Google TV. He adds you as a tester and sends you a link to join the test.
Join the test. Open that link on your phone or computer, signed in to the same Google account, and tap to join.
Install it. After a few hours, search the Play Store on your TV for MFL Football and install it.

body.heading: Set it up once
items: Sign in. Open MFL Football on the TV and point your phone's camera at the QR code. Sign in if it asks, then tap Approve. The TV switches to your board on its own.

Allow the overlay. Open the Score overlay tile. The first time, it asks to show over other apps: press OK and turn it on for MFL Football, then press Back. On some TVs the switch is under Settings › Apps › Special app access › Display over other apps.

No switch on your TV? The tile shows a one-line command instead. Run it once from a computer on the same Wi-Fi, with ADB installed and network debugging turned on in the TV's Developer options: adb shell appops set football.mfl.live SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
Sunday Ticket. If you have NFL Sunday Ticket, tick I have NFL Sunday Ticket in MFL Football settings. The overlay then marks every Sunday afternoon CBS and FOX game as one you can open.

body.heading: While you watch
items: The score bar. Start a game in YouTube TV, then open the Score overlay tile. A thin bar across the top shows every matchup. It never takes the remote, so your TV app keeps working.
The full panel. Open the Score overlay tile again to bring up the panel: your score, win chance and both starting lineups. Left and Right move between your matchups.

Watch your players. The panel's Watch list shows the NFL games your starters are in, live games first. Up and Down pick a game and OK opens it on the TV through your TV's search, where you choose YouTube TV.

Back to the game. Back returns to the score bar, and so does any other button, so the next press reaches your TV app. The panel also drops back to the bar after 30 seconds. To close the overlay altogether, pick Hide overlay at the bottom of the Watch list.

body: The overlay is still new, so tell Brandon what works on your TV and what doesn't.
